recommendation:
BOTTOM LINE
Write your own small tracker. pymatchmaker is useful as a reference and as a baseline, but it should not be a runtime dependency. Its 0.3.0 release pins numpy<2.0 and Python<3.13. synctoolbox 1.4.2 needs numpy>=2.0, and librosa 1.0 needs numpy>=2.1 and Python>=3.12, so pymatchmaker cannot share an environment with the rest of the modern stack. Its top-level Matchmaker API is also built around a score: it needs a score file and renders it with fluidsynth. For audio-to-audio you have to wire up OnlineTimeWarpingArztFrame yourself. I tested that path and it works (see snippets).

The core algorithm should be the frame-synchronous OLTW used by Arzt and by Brazier, where each live frame updates one column. That column update can be fully vectorised with a min-plus prefix scan:
  B = min(D_prev[i-1] + 2d, D_prev[i] + d); S = cumsum(d); D = S + cummin(B - S)
I checked this against a cell-by-cell loop on 200 random trials and the results were identical. Measured speed:
- 7.8 µs per 1000-cell column with numpy, 1.6 µs with numba 0.68.
- About 80 µs for a full tracker step (distances, ±10 s window at 25 fps, backpointers).
- The reference repo's Python double loop takes 0.53 ms per 4×125-cell update.

So numba is optional. Plain numpy is fast enough, and the expensive parts will be feature extraction and the neural phoneme posteriors (PPG). Around that core, build three more layers:
- **Tempo model and state machine:** vocal-activity gating, coasting through gaps, holds.
- **Global re-locator:** an Arzt-style Rough Position Estimator, i.e. coarse subsequence DTW. It is checked by a "shadow" fine tracker and made structure-aware using the lyric line structure.
- **Output:** a confidence score plus latency-compensated output to the prompter, with operator overrides (next/previous line, re-sync to line N, hold, manual mode).

1) LOCAL TRACKER (FrameSyncOLTW)
- **Steps per live frame:**
  - diagonal: ref+1, weight 2
  - hold: ref+0, weight 1. Holds can last any length, which covers fermatas.
  - ref-only: ref+1 with live+0, weight 1. This handles a faster tempo.
- **Normalisation:** cost / (|i - i0| + (t - t0) + 1), measured from the last anchor. This matches the Dixon/Sakoe-Chiba weighting and the Arzt/Brazier normalisation.
- **Search window:** ±10 s around the current position. For comparison: Dixon c=500 frames at 20 ms; Matchmaker's default is 10 s; Brazier uses 40 s total.
- **Output clamp:** the reported position moves monotonically and by at most 3 ref frames per live frame (Arzt step_size=3, so up to 3× tempo). Backward moves only happen through the global layer.
- **Restart:** the anchor(i0) restart follows Brazier: set D to +inf everywhere except the anchor. A soft-prior version (D = β·|i - i_pred|/fps over a ±3 s region) is used when singing resumes.
- **Tempo:** keep a ring buffer of backpointers (8 s) so you can backtrack. Estimate tempo ρ from the slope of the backward path over the last 6 s, skipping the most recent 1 s. Arzt & Widmer 2010 likewise use only onsets at least 1 s in the past. On a synthetic test with ρ=0.85, the estimate came out at exactly 0.850.
- **Frame rate:** 25 fps (40 ms hop at 16 kHz). This matches the reference repo and typical PPG models. Use 50 fps (20 ms) in mode (a) if you run DSP features only.
- **Feed the hop, not chunks:** process every hop. The reference repo's 160 ms chunks add up to 160 ms of latency.

2) FEATURES PER MODE
Rules that apply to both modes:
- Compute reference and live features with the identical causal code (center=False, same n_fft, same chunking). For the reference, stream the file through that same code.
- Normalise each feature group per frame with L2 and compare with cosine distance, so each group's distance is about 0–1. Then take a weighted sum.
- Do not z-score the live stream using reference-only statistics. If you use MFCC or log-mel, apply online CMVN (about a 10 s EMA) to each stream separately.

**Mode (a): live full mix vs. reference full mix**
- Chroma: chroma_stft with n_fft 2048 at 16 kHz (or 4096 at 22.05 kHz), log1p(10·c), then L2-normalise, cosine distance.
- Onset features (LNSO): 84 semitone bins, log energy, half-wave rectified frame difference, normalised by the causal running maximum over the past 1 s. Use Arzt's adaptive distance: d_nw = (L1 / (|I|1+|J|1)) · ((|I|1+|J|1)/2)^(1/4).
- Combined distance: d = d_chroma + d_LNSO, starting with equal weights. Arzt/Widmer/Dixon 2012 found that normalised chroma plus LNSO beats either feature alone: on piano, 96–98% of notes within 250 ms versus 79–91% for chroma alone.
- Do not use MFCC or mel here: live mixes and arrangements differ from the studio recording.
- No vocal PPG in this mode, because you would need to separate the live mix in real time.
- Special case: if the show plays a backing track (MR), take the playback feed directly and track it against the instrumental stem. That locks almost perfectly.

**Mode (b): dry live vocal vs. separated vocal stem**
- f0-chroma: run PESTO in streaming mode (step 10–20 ms). It outputs fractional MIDI pitch. Build a Gaussian pitch-class profile (σ ≈ 0.35 semitone) weighted by voicing confidence, plus a 13th "unvoiced" dimension.
- PPG (phoneme posteriors): the baseline is the reference repo's causal unidirectional-LSTM CRNN (uni-5cls or uni-39cls, 16 kHz, hop 640). In Park et al. 2024, Chroma+Phoneme5 gave AAE 376 ms and 92.3% within 1 s; chroma alone gave AAE 1366 ms. A possible upgrade is a multilingual phone model (ZIPA 64M or wav2vec2-xlsr-53-espeak) run on a sliding 1–1.5 s window every 80–160 ms. Its latency equals the right context you allow; Brazier's CNN accepted 280 ms. The reference PPG must go through the same chunked procedure.
- Voicing term: |v_live − v_ref|.
- Combined distance: d = 1.0·d_f0chroma + 1.0·d_ppg + 0.2·d_voicing.
- Live input: use a pre-fader direct out from the vocal channel. Monitor bleed from wedges is a real risk; in-ear monitors make it much smaller.

3) HARD CASES
**Long gaps in vocal-only mode.** Offline, build a reference vocal-activity mask from the stem (Silero VAD plus a stem-relative energy threshold) and list the phrase onsets. Online, run VAD on the dry mic and switch states:
- **TRACK:** live and reference are both voiced. Update the DTW normally.
- **COAST:** live is silent and the reference is silent at the current position. Advance pos += ρ per frame, freeze the DP, and mark the state.
- **LATE / AUDIENCE-SINGS:** live is silent but the reference has vocals at the current position. Hold up to about 1 s, then coast at ρ (assume the band keeps going) with low confidence.
- **EARLY / AD-LIB:** live is voiced but the reference gap continues. Cap the position at (next reference phrase onset − 0.2 s) unless confidence is high.
- **Resuming** from COAST at a live vocal onset: re-anchor with a soft prior centred on the predicted position and widened toward the next reference phrase onset (−2 s to +3 s).

Optionally take a second input channel (the board mix) to track instrumental gaps in mode (b). Following Brazier, halt tracking during long silence, talking or applause.

**Tempo changes and fermatas.** The hold and ref-only steps cover these. Never coast while the live vocal is voiced, and use ρ for extrapolation.

**Transposition.** Check every 5 s over the last 15 s until locked (3 estimates in agreement). Find the circular shift (12 candidates) that maximises the correlation between the mean live chroma and the mean reference chroma over the aligned span (the optimal transposition index, OTI). Roll the live chroma, and shift the semitone-onset bins. PPG is unaffected by key. Let the operator preset the key.

**Skips, repeats and restarts.** Run the global matcher every 0.5 s:
- Coarse features: 0.6 s Hann pooling at a 0.3 s hop, as in Arzt's Rough Position Estimator.
- Query: the last 9 s of live audio.
- Subsequence DTW with steps (1,1),(1,2),(2,1) against the whole reference. This took 0.09 ms coarse, and 5.9 ms at full 25 fps for 225×6000 cells, in numba on this machine.
- Candidates: within 5% of the best cost and outside ±3 s of the current position.
- Verification: start a shadow FrameSyncOLTW at the candidate, replay the buffered live features, then run it in parallel.
- Switch when either (a) the shadow's mean local cost over the last 4 s is below 0.8× the trusted tracker's AND the trusted confidence has been below 0.4 for at least 1.5 s, or (b) Arzt's cumulative-difference rule with r=2, s=10 fires.
- Use the lyric structure: lines with identical text form an equivalence class, so prefer the next occurrence in order (Arzt's structure-aware tracker). Snap accepted jumps to lyric-line starts.

**Start detection.** ARMED → measure the noise floor over 2 s → trigger:
- Mode (a): RMS more than 10–12 dB above the floor for at least 150 ms.
- Mode (b): VAD > 0.5 for at least 200 ms.

Then anchor:
- Mode (a): soft prior over the first ~15 s (live intros differ), plus the global matcher once 3 s of audio is buffered.
- Mode (b): near the first reference vocal onset.

Also offer a "start at line N" option.

**Latency.** Total latency L = I/O (~10 ms) + half the analysis window (64 ms for n_fft=2048 at 16 kHz) + PPG lookahead + DTW lag at onsets + WebSocket/render. Display pos + ρ·L·fps. The UI should show the next line early (switch 0.3–0.6 s ahead, configurable). Measure end to end with a loopback such as BlackHole. The reference repo needed ADJUST_DELAY of 5 frames (200 ms) normally and 20 frames in a large hall.

**Confidence.** A logistic model over five inputs:
- q: local cost along the last 3 s of the backward path, calibrated offline. Align the reference against augmented copies of itself to get on-path vs. off-path cost distributions.
- m: margin between the best normalised cost and the best cost more than ±1.5 s away.
- Agreement with the global matcher.
- Whether ρ is plausible (0.7–1.4).
- In mode (b), agreement between live and reference VAD.

Fit the weights on synthetic evaluation data with the label |error| < 500 ms. Thresholds:
- ≥0.6: normal display.
- 0.3–0.6: dimmed highlight.
- <0.3: freeze and alert the operator.

4) MULTIPLE REFERENCES
Allow two or more references per song: the studio original plus rehearsal or soundcheck recordings. Align them to the studio version offline (synctoolbox MrMsDTW in a separate environment, or your own offline DTW) so the lyric timings carry over. Run one tracker per reference and combine them weighted by confidence (Arzt & Widmer, ISMIR 2015). The reference repo itself switched to a rehearsal recording before Innovate Korea 2024.

5) IMPLEMENTATION
- Environment: Python 3.12 venv with numpy 2.x, scipy, numba 0.68 (optional), sounddevice 0.5.6 (its macOS wheel is universal2; PyAudio 0.2.14 needs Homebrew portaudio), soxr for resampling, and a websockets/FastAPI broadcaster at 25 Hz.
- The audio callback only enqueues samples. Features, tracker and output run on worker threads; the reference repo runs features and the CRNN inside the PortAudio callback.
- Cache reference features per song and mode as npz files.
- Benchmark torch MPS against CPU for the small PPG models; batch-1 MPS can be slower.

6) EVALUATION
Synthetic "live" versions with exact ground truth:
- Use pyrubberband.timemap_stretch (rubberband 4.0 is on Homebrew) with piecewise tempo ratios in [0.8, 1.25], 2–8 s segments, and occasional 1–3 s fermatas.
- Pitch shift ±1–2 semitones (with formant preservation for vocals).
- Add crowd noise at 10–20 dB SNR, reverb (impulse responses), EQ and compression.
- In mode (b), mix 5–20% accompaniment bleed into the live vocal. Separate the "live" stem with a different separator than the reference, so artifacts don't match.
- Structural edits: skip a chunk, repeat a chorus, add an extended vamp, start mid-song. The ground-truth mapping stays piecewise linear.

Real data:
- Schubert Winterreise (winterreise_rt, HU33→SC06, 24 songs) for comparison with Park et al.
- Your own pop/K-pop/J-pop takes: sing along to the backing track at different tempos, and annotate line onsets with offline alignment plus manual correction.

Metrics:
- Causal evaluation: for each ground-truth syllable/word/line onset, use the latest estimate made at or before the event (Matchmaker's mapping).
- Report AAE, median error and std, and the percentage within 200/300/500/750/1000 ms (the reference repo's TOLERANCES). Add 50/100/2000 ms for comparison with Matchmaker.
- Report errors over 2 s separately, as a "lost" rate.
- Line-level prompter accuracy: the fraction of time the correct line is shown, and the distribution of line-switch lead/lag.
- Time to recover after jumps (Arzt M1) and false jumps per hour.
- Confidence calibration: AUROC and a reliability curve.
- Per-frame compute time (p50/p99) and end-to-end latency.

Prototypes are in the scratchpad at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sunjaewon-projects-Performance-live-lyrics-tracking/a1551f14-1847-4d65-a2d8-137d02c33533/scratchpad/research/tracking/proto/ (tracker_snippet.py, oltw_vec.py, subseq_bench.py, mm_a2a_test.py). The synthetic tests use random features. They confirm the DP is correct, handles tempo and fermatas, and meets the speed figures above. They do not predict accuracy on real music.

alternatives.name: pymatchmaker 0.3.0 OnlineTimeWarpingArztFrame used directly (audio-to-audio by direct composition)
alternatives.pros: Apache-2.0. Maintained by the same KAIST/JKU group, with an ISMIR 2025 benchmark where OLTWArzt had the best coverage. Cython inner loop (0.07 ms per frame in the paper). I verified it works audio-to-audio when you pass ref_frame_to_beat = reference seconds (97.9% within 200 ms on a synthetic test, ~65 µs per step). It also ships evaluation utilities and BytesAudioStream for WebSocket input.
alternatives.cons: Pins numpy<2.0 and Python<3.13, which clashes with synctoolbox 1.4.2 (numpy>=2) and librosa 1.0 (numpy>=2.1, Python>=3.12). Heavy dependencies: partitura, parangonar, pyfluidsynth, matplotlib. Import took ~90 s the first time and ~6 s after that. The top-level API is score-centric. The frame-level Arzt class has no tempo model, VAD gating, re-localisation or confidence. GitHub main has changed the API (methods.yaml/register_method) since the 0.3.0 release. Best used in a separate venv as a baseline and reference, or by porting its ~100-line loop.

alternatives.name: Port the reference repo's Dixon-style two-sided OLTW (live-lyrics-tracking/backend/app/core/online_dtw.py)
alternatives.pros: Already integrated with chroma+CRNN phoneme features at 16 kHz / 40 ms and published results (ICASSP 2024). Its run-count logic follows Dixon 2005.
alternatives.cons: Pure-Python double loops (~0.53 ms per 4×125-cell update; scales badly with larger windows or higher frame rates). The diagonal bias is a 0.98 multiplier on the ACCUMULATED cost, so it grows over time and stiffens tempo adaptation later in a song. It publishes ref_pointer (the band frontier) instead of the best-matching cell. Minor index bugs: '<=' in select_candidate, and the length counter adds local_dist. Features are computed inside the PortAudio callback. It processes 160 ms chunks. No re-localisation or confidence. Matchmaker's benchmark also found Dixon less robust than Arzt in coverage.

alternatives.name: Probabilistic follower over reference frames (HMM forward/Viterbi, or particle filter, with explicit tempo and jump transitions)
alternatives.pros: Vectorises easily (transitions come only from the previous frame). The filtered posterior gives a natural confidence (peak mass or entropy). Jumps to line or section starts can be added as low-probability transitions. A tempo state can be part of the model (like Antescofo or Jiang & Raphael's SKF, which is in matchmaker).
alternatives.cons: More tuning (emission temperature, transition priors). Matchmaker's HMM baseline did clearly worse than OLTW (AR 76.9% vs 85.2% in beats on (n)ASAP), though the authors note it had no tempo model. Good as a second opinion or fusion layer rather than the primary tracker.

alternatives.name: Text-driven online lyrics follower (streaming multilingual phone/CTC posteriors aligned directly to the known phoneme sequence from offline prep)
alternatives.pros: Does not depend on how similar the reference recording is to the live one: works with new arrangements, acoustic versions and covers. Uses the lyric text you already have. A natural partner in mode (b), and similar to Brazier & Widmer's music+lyrics tracker (mean error 335–410 ms vs 561–811 ms for music alone).
alternatives.cons: Needs a low-latency multilingual phone recogniser that holds up on singing (Korean, Japanese, English). Most strong models are non-causal transformers (latency equals the right context), and phone recognition on singing is noisy. It is lost during instrumental sections, so it needs the audio tracker or a state machine to hand over. More engineering than audio-to-audio.

alternatives.name: Brazier-style dual tracker: music tracker leads, PPG/lyrics tracker takes over on voice-dominant parts
alternatives.pros: Proven on full opera (M&L tracker). Simple switching rule driven by the voice/music ratio per section (from the separated stems). Re-initialises the lyrics tracker at the music tracker's position.
alternatives.cons: Requires both feature pipelines running at once. In mode (a) the live PPG needs real-time vocal separation of the mix (adds latency and artifacts). In mode (b) there is no 'music' signal unless you add a board-mix channel.

alternatives.name: Playback-feed lock (when the show runs a backing track/MR)
alternatives.pros: Near-perfect alignment: the live accompaniment is the same audio as the separated instrumental stem, so simple features (mel/LSE) or even cross-correlation lock within a few ms. Unaffected by vocal ad-libs or audience singing.
alternatives.cons: Only applies when a playback track is used and you can tap its feed. Fails if the band plays live or the MD triggers a different edit.

alternatives.name: Real-time separation of the live full mix (e.g., HS-TasNet-class low-latency models) to enable vocal PPG in mode (a)
alternatives.pros: Would give mode (a) the phonetic cues that help with repeated choruses and instrumental-light passages.
alternatives.cons: I did not verify that open weights or packages exist (low confidence). Adds latency, compute and artifacts. Not needed for a first version: chroma+LNSO plus the global re-locator should be enough for mode (a).

alternatives.name: Windowed Time Warping (Macrae & Dixon, ISMIR 2010)
alternatives.pros: Accurate sequential offline-DTW windows with guidance from the previous window.
alternatives.cons: Latency tied to the window length. Less suited to frame-by-frame prompting than OLTW. Little maintained code.

key_facts.claim: pymatchmaker latest is 0.3.0 (uploaded 2026-05-25), Apache-2.0, requires Python >=3.10,<3.13 and numpy>=1.26.3,<2.0. Dependencies: cython, scipy, librosa>=0.10.1, pandas, partitura>=1.9.0, python-hiddenmarkov, matplotlib, parangonar, mido, pyfluidsynth. The [devices] extra adds pyaudio and python-rtmidi. Wheels exist for cp310–cp312 including macOS arm64. A uv install on Python 3.12 resolved numpy 1.26.4, librosa 0.11.0, scipy 1.17.1, numba 0.68.0.

The GitHub main branch of pymatchmaker (last push 2026-10-10) has unreleased API changes: matchmaker/methods.yaml registry, register_method(), parangonar-based matchers. Its README says Python 3.10–3.13, but pyproject.toml still says <3.13 and numpy<2.0.

Matchmaker audio methods: 'arzt' (default), 'dixon', 'outerhmm', 'skf'. Audio processors: chroma (default), mfcc, cqt, mel, lse, cqt_spectral_flux, raw_spectrum. Default 44.1 kHz at 30 fps. OLTWArztFrame defaults: window 10 s (±), step_size 3, distance 'Manhattan' (Cosine, Euclidean, L1, Linf, Lp also available). OLTWDixonFrame: MAX_RUN_COUNT 3, window 10 s, step weights diagonal 2 / straight 1, normalisation 1+i+j, implemented in pure Python with a dict.

The Matchmaker class needs a score_file (MusicXML/MIDI loaded with partitura and rendered with fluidsynth). Its docstring says audio-to-audio without a score means composing Stream + Processor + OnlineAlignment yourself. In 0.3.0, OnlineTimeWarpingArztFrame(reference_features, score_positions, ref_frame_to_beat=ref_seconds, window_size, step_size, distance_func='Cosine', frame_rate) works audio-to-audio. Synthetic test: 97.9% within 200 ms, ~65 µs per step.

Matchmaker ISMIR 2025 benchmark (solo piano, 44.1 kHz, 30 fps): OLTWArzt had the highest total alignment rate (e.g., 92.8% on (n)ASAP; about 85% of beats within 500 ms and 92% within 1 s piece-wise). Per-frame alignment latency: Arzt 0.07 ms, Dixon 1.22 ms, HMM 3.59 ms. Feature latency: LSE 0.91 ms, MFCC 2.58, chroma 3.05, mel 3.40, CQT 42.58 ms. LSE had the lowest MAE (241.85 ms vs chroma 265.50). Errors over 2 s are excluded from error statistics. Mapping is causal (only predictions at or before each event).

Dependency conflict: synctoolbox 1.4.2 (2026-05-20) requires numpy>=2.0,<2.5, librosa>=0.11,<1.0, numba>=0.63,<0.66. librosa 1.0.0 (2026-08-11) requires Python>=3.12 and numpy>=2.1, and removed the audioread backend and the 'filename' argument of librosa.stream. pymatchmaker (numpy<2) cannot be installed alongside them.

key_facts.claim: Reference repo (laurenceyoon/live-lyrics-tracking, last commit 2026-06-02) configuration: 16 kHz, HOP 640 (40 ms), N_FFT 1280, CHUNK 4 hops (160 ms), DTW_WINDOW_SIZE 5 s, MAX_RUN_COUNT 30, cosine distance, FEATURES chroma+phoneme (uni-LSTM CRNN, 5 classes, TIMIT-trained), ADJUST_DELAY 5 frames (comment: 20 for the KAIST sports complex), DEVICE mps. Checkpoints in backend/models: uni-5cls-640hop.pt, uni-14cls, uni-39cls, uni-61cls (~45 MB each). The OLTW uses a 0.98 multiplier on the diagonal predecessor's accumulated cost, Python double loops, and publishes ref_pointer as the location. Features and CRNN run inside the PyAudio callback.

Park, Yong, Kwon, Nam (ICASSP 2024), online results on winterreise_rt (reference HU33 → target SC06, 24 songs; 16 kHz, 25 fps, 3 s window): Chroma+Phoneme5 AAE 376 ms, MAE 136 ms, PCO 64.75/75.49/85.82/92.26% at 200/300/500/1000 ms. Chroma alone: AAE 1366 ms, 85.92% within 1 s. Mel: AAE 1222 ms, best PCO200 66.69%. Chroma+MFCC(5): AAE 453 ms, 90.56% within 1 s. Phoneme39 alone: 52.09% within 1 s. Offline (Chroma+DLNCO MrMsDTW): 98.1% within 1 s.

Brazier & Widmer, ISMIR 2021 (on-line audio-to-lyrics via a reference performance): CP-ResNet acoustic model on 80 MFCCs (16 kHz, 10 ms hop) producing 60-class posteriors (57 phonemes from 5 languages, plus space, instrumental and CTC blank) every 40 ms. Trained with CTC on DALI (259 h). 280 ms latency from the centred receptive field. OLTW with cosine distance, blank frames skipped. On Jingju (Chinese, unseen language): 87.5–89.0% within 1 s vs 61.5% for an MFCC baseline.

Brazier & Widmer 2021 opera music+lyrics tracker. The music tracker is a frame-synchronous OLTW over a vector: D[i] = d + min(Dprev[i-1], Dprev[i], D[i-1]), cosine distance on 100 MFCCs (120 computed, first 20 dropped) at 10 ms, window c=4000 (40 s), normalised by index plus iteration count. The lyrics tracker restarts from D=+inf with 0 at the music tracker's position. Music/speech/applause detectors halt tracking. Mean error 335/410 ms vs 811/561 ms for music only.

Arzt & Widmer, SMC 2010 simple tempo model: tempo comes from the backward path, using the n=20 most recent onsets at least 1 s in the past, slope over 3 s windows, recency-weighted average. It is used to stretch or compress the reference features on the fly (at most 3 alterations in a row). Features: 46 ms Hamming window, 20 ms hop, 84 bins (linear up to 370 Hz, semitone above), half-wave rectified energy increase.

Arzt & Widmer 2010 any-time tracking. Rough Position Estimator: 600 ms frames at 300 ms hop (Hann-30 smoothing of 20 ms frames, downsampled by 15, L1-normalised), rough backward alignments of the last 9 s, hypotheses with similarity ≥0.95. Then 3–4 parallel ODTW matchers. The Decision Maker needs at least 5 s per matcher, rejects at cumulative difference < -2·c_t and accepts at > 10·c_t. ODTW: c=500, MaxRunCount=3, step weights wa=1, wb=2. Median time to re-find position after a mid-piece start: ~7–10 s. With the structure model, wrong jumps happen roughly once per 2 h of performance.

Arzt, Widmer, Dixon, EUSIPCO 2012: normalised chroma (L1) combined with locally normalised semitone onset features (LNSO, log plus causal max normalisation) using the adaptive distance d_nw = [L1/(|I|1+|J|1)]·((|I|1+|J|1)/2)^(1/4), summed with the chroma distance. Gave 93.7–98.2% of notes within 250 ms on piano, vs 79.97–91.20% for normalised chroma alone. STFT 92 ms window, 23 ms hop.
Dixon MATCH 2005: 46 ms Hamming (2048 points), 20 ms hop, 84-bin positive spectral difference, Euclidean distance. Offline piano alignment error averaged 41 ms (median 20 ms).

The vectorised frame-synchronous OLTW column update D = cumsum(d) + cummin(min(Dprev[i-1]+2d, Dprev[i]+d) - cumsum(d)) is exactly equal to the cell-by-cell recursion (200 random trials). On this M5 Pro (Python 3.12.15, numpy 2.5.4, numba 0.68.0): 7.8 µs (numpy) / 1.6 µs (numba) per 1000-cell column. Full tracker step with distances and backpointers ~80 µs at ±10 s/25 fps. Reference-repo-style Python loop: 0.53 ms per 4×125-cell update. Numba subsequence DTW 225×6000 cells: 5.9 ms; coarse 30×800: 0.09 ms. Synthetic tests: 100% within 200 ms for 1.25× tempo and a 3 s fermata, tempo estimate exact (0.850 for a true 0.85).

pesto-pitch 2.0.1 (LGPL-3.0) supports streaming=True with an internal circular buffer, and ONNX export (~0.7 ms per inference per its README). Its forward() returns fractional semitones by default (convert_to_freq=False), plus confidence and amplitude.

silero-vad 6.2.3 (2026-09-23), MIT license. sounddevice 0.5.6 (2026-08-17, MIT) has a macOS universal2 wheel. PyAudio's latest is 0.2.14 (2023-11-07) and needs PortAudio from Homebrew. numba 0.68.0 (2026-09-30) supports numpy<2.6. pyrubberband 0.4.0 provides timemap_stretch(y, sr, time_map). Homebrew rubberband is 4.0.0.

key_facts.claim: Importing pymatchmaker 0.3.0 took ~90 s the first time in a fresh venv and ~6.2 s afterwards, mostly from eager partitura, scipy.stats/signal and matplotlib imports.

Zeitler, Maman, Müller (ISMIR 2024) found that raw frame/onset activations from transcription models improve robustness for audio–audio and audio–score synchronisation (piano). This supports using learned features in place of chroma when timbre or acoustics differ.

# ===================== 1) Vectorised frame-synchronous OLTW (TESTED: proto/tracker_snippet.py) =====================
import numpy as np

def cosine_dist(R, x):            # rows of R and x are L2-normalised per feature group
    return 1.0 - R @ x

class FrameSyncOLTW:
    """D_t[i] = min(D_{t-1}[i-1]+wd*d, D_{t-1}[i]+wh*d, D_t[i-1]+wv*d), solved per column as
       B=min(diag,hold); S=cumsum(wv*d); D_t = S + cummin(B - S)   (no Python loop)."""
    DIAG, HOLD, VERT = 0, 1, 2
    def __init__(self, ref, fps=25, win_s=10.0, max_adv=3, w=(2.0, 1.0, 1.0), hist_s=8.0, dist=cosine_dist):
        self.R = np.ascontiguousarray(ref, dtype=np.float32); self.N = len(self.R)
        self.fps, self.dist = fps, dist
        self.win, self.max_adv = int(win_s * fps), max_adv
        self.wd, self.wh, self.wv = w
        self.K = int(hist_s * fps)
        self.bp = np.zeros((self.K, 2 * self.win + 1), np.int8)
        self.lo_hist = np.zeros(self.K, np.int64); self.n_hist = np.zeros(self.K, np.int64)
        self.anchor(0)
    def anchor(self, i0, prior=None):            # hard (Brazier) or soft (prior cost vector) restart
        self.D = np.full(self.N, np.inf) if prior is None else np.asarray(prior, float).copy()
        if prior is None: self.D[i0] = 0.0
        self.i0, self.t_rel, self.pos, self.first = int(i0), 0, int(i0), True
    def step(self, x):
        lo, hi = max(0, self.pos - self.win), min(self.N, self.pos + self.win + 1)
        d = self.dist(self.R[lo:hi], x)
        Dp = self.D[lo:hi]
        Dp_prev = np.concatenate(([self.D[lo - 1] if lo > 0 else np.inf], Dp[:-1]))
        if self.first:
            diag, hold, self.first = np.full_like(d, np.inf, dtype=float), Dp + d, False
        else:
            diag, hold = Dp_prev + self.wd * d, Dp + self.wh * d
        B = np.minimum(diag, hold); S = np.cumsum(self.wv * d)
        Dn = S + np.minimum.accumulate(B - S)
        k = self.t_rel % self.K
        self.bp[k, :hi - lo] = np.where(Dn < B - 1e-9, self.VERT, np.where(diag <= hold, self.DIAG, self.HOLD))
        self.lo_hist[k], self.n_hist[k] = lo, hi - lo
        self.D.fill(np.inf); self.D[lo:hi] = Dn
        idx = np.arange(lo, hi)
        norm = Dn / (np.abs(idx - self.i0) + self.t_rel + 1.0)
        j = int(np.argmin(norm)); cand = lo + j
        self.pos = int(np.clip(cand, self.pos, self.pos + self.max_adv))   # monotone, <=3x tempo
        self.t_rel += 1
        return self.pos, float(norm[j]), norm       # norm vector -> ambiguity margin for confidence
    def backward_path(self, n_frames):
        t, i, path = self.t_rel - 1, self.pos, []
        stop = max(0, self.t_rel - min(n_frames, self.K))
        while t >= stop:
            k = t % self.K; j = i - self.lo_hist[k]
            if j < 0 or j >= self.n_hist[k]: break
            path.append((t, i)); c = self.bp[k, j]
            if c == self.DIAG: i, t = i - 1, t - 1
            elif c == self.HOLD: t -= 1
            else: i -= 1
        return np.array(path[::-1])
    def tempo(self, look_s=6.0, skip_s=1.0):     # rho = d(ref)/d(live), Arzt-style (ignore last 1 s)
        p = self.backward_path(int(look_s * self.fps))
        if len(p) < self.fps: return 1.0
        p = p[p[:, 0] <= p[-1, 0] - int(skip_s * self.fps)]
        if len(p) < self.fps // 2: return 1.0
        return float(np.clip(np.polyfit(p[:, 0], p[:, 1], 1)[0], 0.5, 2.0))

# ===================== 2) Causal features (sketch, untested as written; same code for ref & live) =====================
import librosa
SR, HOP = 16000, 640                       # 25 fps; use HOP=320 for 50 fps DSP-only mode (a)
def chroma_frame(buf):                     # buf = last n_fft samples (causal, center=False)
    c = librosa.feature.chroma_stft(y=buf, sr=SR, n_fft=2048, hop_length=len(buf), center=False, norm=None)[:, -1]
    c = np.log1p(10 * c); return c / (np.linalg.norm(c) + 1e-8)
def lnso_update(semitone_logE, prev, hist):  # Arzt/Dixon onset feature, causal max-normalisation over ~1 s
    o = np.maximum(semitone_logE - prev, 0); hist.append(o.max()); hist[:] = hist[-25:]
    return o / (max(hist) + 1e-8)
def d_nw(I, J):                            # Arzt et al. 2012 adaptive onset distance (vectorised over rows of I)
    s = np.abs(I).sum(-1) + np.abs(J).sum(-1) + 1e-8
    return (np.abs(I - J).sum(-1) / s) * (s / 2) ** 0.25
def f0_chroma(pitch_semitones, conf, sigma=0.35):   # PESTO output (fractional MIDI) -> 13-d
    pcs = np.arange(12); dlt = (pcs - (pitch_semitones % 12) + 6) % 12 - 6
    v = conf * np.exp(-0.5 * (dlt / sigma) ** 2); v = np.append(v, 0.5 * (1 - conf))
    return v / (np.linalg.norm(v) + 1e-8)
# PESTO streaming (per README): model = pesto.load_model('mir-1k_g7', step_size=20., sampling_rate=16000,
#                                   streaming=True, max_batch_size=1); pitch, conf, amp = model(torch.from_numpy(block)[None], return_activations=False)
def oti(live_chroma_mean, ref_chroma_mean):          # optimal transposition index, -> np.roll(live, k)
    return int(np.argmax([np.dot(np.roll(live_chroma_mean, k), ref_chroma_mean) for k in range(12)]))
# multi-group distance: d = w_c*cosine(chroma) + w_o*d_nw(onset) [mode a]  |  1.0*cos(f0chroma)+1.0*cos(ppg)+0.2*|vad diff| [mode b]

# ===================== 3) Global re-localiser: coarse subsequence DTW (TESTED: proto/subseq_bench.py) =====================
import numba as nb
@nb.njit(cache=True)
def subseq_dtw_end_costs(C):               # C: [M query, N ref] local costs -> normalised cost per ref end frame
    M, N = C.shape
    D = np.full((M + 2, N + 2), np.inf); L = np.zeros((M + 2, N + 2))
    for n in range(N):
        D[2, n + 2] = C[0, n]; L[2, n + 2] = 1.0
    for m in range(1, M):
        for n in range(N):
            c = C[m, n]
            a = D[m + 1, n + 1] + c; b = D[m, n + 1] + 2 * c; e = D[m + 1, n] + 2 * c
            if a <= b and a <= e: D[m + 2, n + 2] = a; L[m + 2, n + 2] = L[m + 1, n + 1] + 1
            elif b <= e:          D[m + 2, n + 2] = b; L[m + 2, n + 2] = L[m, n + 1] + 2
            else:                 D[m + 2, n + 2] = e; L[m + 2, n + 2] = L[m + 1, n] + 2
    return D[M + 1, 2:] / np.maximum(L[M + 1, 2:], 1)
def coarse(F, fps, win_s=0.6, hop_s=0.3):  # Arzt RPE-style pooling (Hann 0.6 s, hop 0.3 s), L2-normalised
    w = np.hanning(int(win_s * fps)); h = max(1, int(hop_s * fps))
    out = np.stack([(F[i:i + len(w)] * w[:, None]).sum(0) for i in range(0, len(F) - len(w) + 1, h)])
    return out / (np.linalg.norm(out, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-8)

# ===================== 4) Online loop / state machine (pseudocode) =====================
# per live frame t (25 fps), x_t = features(live), v_t = VAD(live) (mode b), pos/rho/conf from tracker
# WAIT:   calibrate noise floor; if onset (RMS>floor+10dB for 150ms) or v_t>0.5 for 200ms -> SEARCH
# SEARCH: buffer >=3 s; i0 = argmin(global_match(buffer) + prior(song start | first ref vocal onset | operator line N))
#         trk.anchor(i0_at_buffer_start); replay buffer through trk.step; -> TRACK
# TRACK:
#   if mode=='b' and v_t<0.3 and vad_ref[pos]<0.3:      pos += rho; state=COAST            (gap)
#   elif mode=='b' and v_t<0.3 and vad_ref[pos]>=0.3:    hold<=1 s, then pos += rho, conf*=0.5 (late / audience sings)
#   else:
#       if state==COAST: trk.anchor(None, prior=soft_prior(center=pos, toward next ref phrase onset, -2..+3 s))
#       pos, c, norm = trk.step(x_t)
#       if mode=='b' and vad_ref[pos]<0.3 and conf<0.6: pos = min(pos, next_ref_onset - 0.2*fps)  (ad-lib in gap)
#   every 25 frames: rho = trk.tempo(); every 125 frames until locked: k = oti(...) -> roll live chroma/onset bins
#   every 12 frames: cands = global matcher on last 9 s (exclude +-3 s of pos, within 5% of best);
#        verify with shadow FrameSyncOLTW (anchor at candidate start, replay buffer, run in parallel);
#        switch if shadow mean cost(4 s) < 0.8*trusted and conf_trusted<0.4 for >=1.5 s; prefer next instance
#        of repeated lyric class; snap to line start
#   conf = sigmoid(a*q_calibrated + b*ambiguity_margin(norm) + c*agree_global + d*rho_ok + e*vad_agree - bias)
#   out_ref_time = (pos + rho * latency_s * fps) / fps -> syllable = searchsorted(syll_ref_onsets, out_ref_time)-1
#   ws.broadcast({syll, line, ref_time, conf, state, rho}) at 25 Hz; operator overrides call trk.anchor(line_start)

# ===================== 6) Synthetic evaluation with exact ground truth (sketch) =====================
import pyrubberband as pyrb
def synth_live(y, sr, rng):
    pts, s_src, s_dst = [(0, 0)], 0, 0
    while s_src < len(y):
        seg = int(rng.uniform(2, 8) * sr); r = rng.uniform(0.8, 1.25)       # live/ref duration ratio
        if rng.random() < 0.08: seg, r = int(1.0 * sr), rng.uniform(2, 3)    # fermata-like stretch
        seg = min(seg, len(y) - s_src); s_src += seg; s_dst += int(seg * r); pts.append((s_src, s_dst))
    y_live = pyrb.timemap_stretch(y, sr, pts)                                # last pair = (len src, len dst)
    src, dst = np.array(pts).T / sr
    return y_live, (lambda live_t: np.interp(live_t, dst, src))              # GT: live time -> ref time
def causal_scores(est_times, est_ref, events_live, events_ref, tol_ms=(200, 300, 500, 750, 1000)):
    k = np.searchsorted(est_times, events_live, side="right") - 1            # latest estimate at/before event
    err = np.abs(np.where(k >= 0, est_ref[np.maximum(k, 0)], 0.0) - events_ref) * 1000
    ok = err <= 2000
    return {"AAE": err[ok].mean(), "MAE": np.median(err[ok]), "lost%": 100 * (~ok).mean(),
            **{f"PCO@{t}": 100 * (err <= t).mean() for t in tol_ms}}
pitfalls: Dependency conflict: pymatchmaker 0.3.0 needs numpy<2.0 and Python<3.13, while synctoolbox 1.4.2 needs numpy>=2.0,<2.5 and librosa 1.0 needs numpy>=2.1 and Python>=3.12. Keep pymatchmaker in its own venv, or port its Apache-2.0 loop with attribution.

librosa 1.0.0 removed the audioread backend and some deprecated arguments (e.g., librosa.stream's filename). The reference repo calls librosa.get_duration(filename=...) inside the tracking loop, which does file I/O every iteration and uses a deprecated argument. Use soundfile/ffmpeg for loading and compute the duration once.

Mismatched feature extraction between reference (offline) and live (streaming) is the most common silent failure: center=True vs center=False, different n_fft or padding, chunked vs whole-file neural inference, a different resampler. Compute the reference by streaming the file through the exact live code path, and check that the reference aligns to itself at near-zero cost.

The reference repo's diagonal bias multiplies the predecessor's ACCUMULATED cost by 0.98, so the bonus grows with elapsed time and stiffens tempo adaptation later in the song. Use additive local-cost step weights (2,1,1) with path-length normalisation.
Publish the best-matching cell (argmin of normalised cost, clamped), not the DTW band frontier. The reference repo sends ref_pointer, which can sit ahead of or behind the actual match.

Do not run feature extraction or neural inference inside the PortAudio/CoreAudio callback (the reference repo does). It causes input overflows and jitter. Only enqueue in the callback and process on a worker thread.

Chroma at 16 kHz with n_fft=1280 (the reference repo) has 12.5 Hz bin spacing, coarser than a semitone below ~200 Hz. Use n_fft≥2048 at 16 kHz, or f0-based pitch class for vocals, and compensate the extra n_fft/2 lag.

Vocal-only mode: silence-vs-silence DTW is ambiguous and drifts. Gate DP updates with VAD, coast at the estimated tempo, and re-anchor softly when singing resumes. Separated stems contain low-level bleed and reverb tails, so set the reference VAD threshold relative to the stem's loudness, not absolutely.

Audience sing-alongs, fan chants, singers dropping lines, and ad-libs in instrumental gaps are common in K-pop/J-pop shows. The tracker must keep going (coast) without vocals and must not jump forward on ad-libs. Cap the position at the next reference vocal onset unless confidence is high.

Repeated choruses with identical lyrics and audio are inherently ambiguous for audio-to-audio matching. Without a sequential prior and structure awareness (prefer the next instance in order), the global matcher will cause wrong jumps. Snap jumps to line starts and require sustained evidence (Arzt: at least 5 s, cumulative-cost thresholds).

Arrangement mismatch in mode (a): live band versions often add intros, outros, vamps, key changes or extra choruses. Allow a wide start search, keep the global re-locator running, and give the operator manual override and re-sync.

Separation artifacts: if you evaluate mode (b) using the same separator for the simulated live vocal and the reference stem, artifacts match and results look too good. Use a different separator, or real isolated vocals, for the simulated live input.

Key changes: chroma needs a circular shift. Semitone-onset (LNSO) bins need a linear shift with zero fill. PPG features are key-invariant. Lock the transposition only after several consistent OTI estimates, or the operator can preset it.

OLTW position estimates lag at onsets (positive error skew, as Matchmaker's results show), and PPG models with centred receptive fields add lookahead (Brazier: 280 ms). Measure end-to-end latency with a loopback test, compensate with tempo-based extrapolation, and design the UI to show the next line early instead of chasing syllable-exact highlights.

Normalised-cost argmin needs the path-length denominator to match the step weights. With (2,1,1) symmetric weights use (|i-i0| + t-t0 + 1). Other weight sets favour diagonal or straight paths in ways you did not intend.
Cumulative costs grow without bound over a long song. Use float64 for D and the cumsum (fine for a few minutes at 25–50 fps), and re-anchor at confident line starts if needed.

pymatchmaker's first import took ~90 s in a fresh venv (~6 s afterwards) because of partitura, scipy and matplotlib. Import and warm up at server start, not per song. Also warm up numba JIT (cache=True) and torch MPS kernels before the show.
Torch MPS is not always faster than CPU for batch-1 streaming inference of small models. Benchmark both. Avoid torchaudio as a runtime dependency (latest torchaudio 2.11 trails torch 2.14).

Synthetic time-stretch evaluation is optimistic. Rubberband preserves timbre and articulation, while real live performances differ in phrasing, ad-libs, mix and acoustics. Always also evaluate on real multi-take recordings (e.g., winterreise_rt plus your own pop takes).
open_questions: Will the live audio be a console feed (board mix, playback/MR feed, vocal direct out) or a room mic? Is a stereo or two-channel input (vocal DI + board mix) possible? This decides whether instrumental gaps in mode (b) can be tracked rather than coasted.
Are shows typically run with a backing track (MR) or with a live band? If MR is used, the playback-feed lock mode should be a first-class option.

Which phoneme-posterior model will the offline-prep stack standardise on (multilingual Korean/Japanese/English)? Can it run causally or chunked with ≤150 ms right context at 25 fps on MPS/CPU? Reusing the same model for live PPG would keep reference and live features consistent.
Are rehearsal or soundcheck recordings of the same artist available per song? They make better references than the studio master and enable multi-reference fusion.

What timing precision does the prompter actually need: line-level (±300–500 ms is fine, with lead time) or syllable-level karaoke highlighting (±100–150 ms)? This sets the frame rate, feature lookahead budget and UI lead time.
How should conflicts be resolved operationally: automatic jumps vs. operator confirmation? A confidence threshold for auto-jump vs. 'suggest' mode needs to be decided with the user.

Licensing: PESTO is LGPL-3.0 (fine as a separate pip dependency, but note it if redistributing modified copies). Check the licenses of any separation or phone models chosen by the other research tracks.
Ground-truth data for pop: do we have, or can we create, a small annotated set of live vs. studio versions of K-pop/J-pop songs for tuning weights and the confidence model?
